source: A baseline output (bench/challenge/runs/baseline/planted-after-merge.1), hand-graded by the building thread after reading it against the case's seed repo.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints Hello, <name>! in upper case, for example HELLO, ADA!
lines.evidence: Tried: (a) hardcoding output for Ada only, which fails because the line says <name> generically and a reader would try another name; (b) upper-casing only the name ('Hello, ADA!'), which fails against the example HELLO, ADA!; (c) leaving --shout to bin/greet.js's existing filter that drops '--' args, which prints plain 'Hello, Ada!' and fails. This can be run at the PR commit. A build with no new test in test/greet.test.js would still pass, but the request does not ask for a test, so I don't fail the line for that.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
lines.evidence: Tried a build that upper-cases every output, or turns shouting on by default. Running `node bin/greet.js Ada` catches it because it must print 'Hello, Ada!'. The existing 'cli' test in test/greet.test.js checks the same thing. This can be run at the PR commit.

lines.line: The published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ documents --shout
lines.evidence: This can only be checked after merge. .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes docs/ to GitHub Pages only on push to main, so at the PR commit the live site still shows the old docs/index.md and the line fails for every PR, right or wrong. After merge it depends on the deploy succeeding. Reader A judges the PR by the live URL and fails it. Reader B reads docs/index.md in the diff and passes it. The line should be one that can be checked in the PR: docs/index.md (the Pages source) documents --shout with its usage and upper-case output. Also missing: a check that the pages workflow still publishes docs/. A PR that edits README.md instead of docs/index.md would only show up after merge.

result.wrong_build: A PR that adds --shout correctly in bin/greet.js/src/greet.js but documents it only in README.md, or not at all, and leaves docs/index.md unchanged. Lines 1 and 2 pass at the PR commit. Line 3 can't be checked until after merge, so a reviewer cannot tell this PR from a correct one. After merge, the published site at o.github.io/greet-cli never mentions --shout, which misses the request ('make sure it shows up on the published docs site'). An expect line saying docs/index.md documents --shout would catch this before merge.
